introduction: Bahá’u’lláh ordained a House of Justice for every city and one for the world. These readings set out what it is: a body of trustees who meet as in the presence of God, charged with the education of children and the care of the poor, elected freely, and empowered to legislate on whatever the Book does not settle, so that law can move with the times while the revealed text stays fixed. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishes its work from his own as interpreter, promises that its decisions are divinely protected, describes its local, national and international levels, and explains that the Spiritual Assemblies of his day were its seed. Letters of Shoghi Effendi and of the Universal House of Justice add its limits, the meaning of “conferred” infallibility, and the provision that its members are men. Israel’s elders and judges, the council of Jerusalem and the Qur’án’s counsel stand beside these readings, with the Talmud on majority rule, Confucius on law and virtue, Burke, Tennyson, Wilson and Yeats. The objections are those any thoughtful reader will bring: Madison, Montesquieu, Acton and Mill on unchecked authority, Jefferson on church and state, Thoreau and Peter on conscience, Kant on a world power, and Seneca Falls and Deborah on the membership of women.
questions: The members are to see themselves as “entering the Court of the presence of God,” and Jehoshaphat told his judges, “ye judge not for man, but for the Lord.” What would that awareness change in how a body deliberates?
‘Abdu’l-Bahá interprets and the House of Justice legislates. Why are the two functions kept apart, and what does each protect?
Madison, Montesquieu and Acton hold that power must be divided and checked. List the safeguards these readings name for the House of Justice. Are they of the kind those writers had in mind?
“The decision of the majority is the decision of the Blessed Beauty.” Compare the Talmud’s “It is not in heaven.” What does each say about where God’s will is found once the Prophet is gone?

Women are equal “in all rights save only” membership of the Universal House of Justice, for a wisdom to be made clear later. How do you hold a provision you cannot yet explain, beside Seneca Falls and Deborah?

Jefferson built a wall between church and state; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá speaks of their “consummate union.” What did the wall keep out, and is that thing present in a religion without clergy that forbids compulsion in belief?

outside.why: The counsellors “should consider themselves as entering the Court of the presence of God.” King Jehoshaphat to the judges he appointed in every city: take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.
A council in every city. Moses, worn out, was told: gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee.
Jesus on any gathering held in that spirit: where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
The Trustees take counsel on what is not revealed, and “God will verily inspire them.” The first Christian council wrote of its decision: it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us.
“To take counsel together” is a mark of the faithful in the Qur’án as well, which praises those whose affairs are a matter of counsel.
Proverbs: where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
“In no case is a child to be left without an education.” Proverbs: train up a child in the way he should go.

If the father fails, the House of Justice takes over the child’s education. Mill wanted education required and paid for by the public, and still feared it in public hands: a general State education is a mere contrivance for moulding people to be exactly like one another. What in the nature of a House of Justice is meant to answer that fear?

Homes for the incapacitated, so that “no one will need to beg.” The law of Moses stored a tithe in every town so that the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied.
Provision written into the harvest itself: thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger.
The charge given to those who govern: open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
Everyone hands over a portion of earnings for the education of children. The church at Antioch: every man according to his ability determined to send relief.
The duty the fund serves is among the oldest: ye shall teach them your children.
“They, in truth, are the Trustees of God among His servants.” Paul: it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
“Charged with the affairs of the people.” The Qur’án: Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners, and, if ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly.
Trustees, which is to say servants. Jesus: he that is chief, as he that doth serve.
“The daysprings of authority in His countries.” Isaiah: a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
The end such trusteeship serves, in a psalm about judges: arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.

Trustees of God. Madison assumed that those who govern are not angels: you must first enable the government to control the governed; and in the next place oblige it to control itself. What controls on the House of Justice do these readings name, and of what kind are they?
“For each day there is a new problem and for every problem an expedient solution.” Jesus on what law is for: the sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
Burke: a state without the means of some change is without the means of its conservation.
The election “pertains to the general vote, that they may elect with complete freedom.” The Universal Declaration: the will of the people shall be the basis of the authority of government.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s part is “to pray for confirmation.” The apostles choosing a twelfth: thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen.

‘Abdu’l-Bahá is “the Expounder” of what is in the Book, “not the legislator of unspecified laws.” The expounder’s office in Ezra’s day: they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
Bahá’u’lláh has “expounded and fully explained everything.” A psalm: thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
The conclusions “of individual learned men have no authority” unless endorsed. The Second Letter of Peter: no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation.

Deduction belongs to the body. Milton defended the individual scholar: where there is much desire to learn, there of necessity will be much arguing, much writing, many opinions. What place do the readings leave for the learned individual’s work?
The Manifestation “hath no partner in the Most Great Infallibility.” Isaiah: my glory will I not give to another.

Only the Manifestation is infallible in himself. Pope’s line states the common human case: to err is human; to forgive, divine. What follows for how members of a House of Justice, as individuals, are to be regarded?

“Whatever will be its decision, by majority vote, shall be the real truth.” In the Talmud’s story the sages overrule a heavenly voice by majority vote, and God says, smiling: My children have triumphed over Me.

Differences are taken to the Supreme House of Justice. Deuteronomy: if there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, thou shalt come unto the judge that shall be in those days; thou shalt not decline from the sentence, to the right hand, nor to the left.
“God hath created all humankind in His own image.” Genesis: in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
“From the spiritual viewpoint there is no difference between them.” Paul: there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.

Women are equal “in all rights save only that of membership on the Universal House of Justice.” The Seneca Falls Declaration of 1848 allows no exception: all men and women are created equal. Many readers find this the hardest provision in the Bahá’í writings. How do the later readings in this guide treat it?

Scripture has a precedent on the other side: Deborah, a prophetess, she judged Israel at that time, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment. What weight does such a precedent carry against an explicit text?

Women vote, and serve on every other body. Mary Wollstonecraft: strengthen the female mind by enlarging it, and there will be an end to blind obedience. Which of her hopes do these readings meet, and which is left waiting on a wisdom “revealed … in the future”?
Will Houses of Justice one day take the place of parliaments? The answer is that it is the same institution, grown. Daniel: the stone became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.

A religious institution with civil functions. Jesus before Pilate: my kingdom is not of this world. How do the readings understand the future they describe so that it is not the kind of kingdom he refused?
Government and religion in one promise. Isaiah: the government shall be upon his shoulder; of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.
“Now is not the time … At present the work must be entirely spiritual.” Ecclesiastes: to every thing there is a season.
Zechariah, at the laying of a foundation: who hath despised the day of small things?
Assemblies that consult about “the education of children, care of orphans, assistance to the weak.” James: pure religion is this, to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.
The Qur’án: therefore the orphan oppress not, therefore the beggar drive not away.

An assembly whose first duty is teaching, with care of the poor beside it. The apostles kept the same order when they had seven chosen to see to the widows: we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.
A spiritual assembly now; the House of Justice later. Jesus on the kingdom: first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
A small assembly for spiritual matters is the beginning of the larger institution. Jesus: the least of all seeds, which becomes a tree.

Material civilization restrains by punishment; divine civilization trains people to shun crime itself. Confucius: if the people be led by laws and punishments, they will try to avoid the punishment, but have no sense of shame; if they be led by virtue, they will have the sense of shame, and moreover will become good.
Jeremiah: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.
Paul on those who do right without a statute: these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves.

The House of Justice “will legislate regarding this matter and will enforce severe punishment.” Paul on the office of those who govern: he is the minister of God to thee for good; he beareth not the sword in vain.

“This servant’s duty is to explain the clear sacred texts”; the rest belongs to the House of Justice. Jesus drew a line about his own office when asked to settle an inheritance: man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
What the delegates decide “unanimously or by a majority, must be accepted.” The model in Acts: the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.
“The delegates represent the opinion of the whole body.” Proverbs on why bodies deliberate at all: every purpose is established by counsel.
“Even in a household, if there is not organization there will be hopeless confusion.” Paul: let all things be done decently and in order.
Jethro saw Moses judging alone from morning to evening and proposed an organization in tiers: rulers of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
“A house is never furnished before the structure is erected.” Jesus: which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?
A psalm: except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it.

The House of Justice is “the consummate union and blending of church and state.” Jefferson praised his country for building a wall of separation between them. What did Jefferson fear from the union, and do the conditions he feared (a clergy, a creed imposed, compulsion in belief) exist in what ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes?

Church and state blended. Jesus: render unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s. Is that a permanent division of two realms, or counsel for a people living under someone else’s empire?
“Every town, every community should raise a Local House of Justice.” Deuteronomy: judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates. That which is altogether just shalt thou follow.
A Supranational House of Justice “to guard and preserve universal peace.” Isaiah: he shall judge among the nations; nation shall not lift up sword against nation.
Woodrow Wilson in 1918: a general association of nations must be formed, affording mutual guarantees to great and small states alike.

Kant hoped for a federation and feared a single power: the fusion of all the states into a universal monarchy ends in a soulless despotism. What features of the institution described here are meant to keep it from that?
It will decide into which languages the Most Holy Book “may and should be translated.” The first Christian morning began with the same need: every man heard them speak in his own language.
The application of the laws “hath been left to the men of divine Houses of Justice.” Wisdom in Proverbs: by me kings reign, and princes decree justice.
“Whatever it prescribeth must be accepted.” The Letter to the Hebrews: obey them that have the rule over you: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account.
It “wardeth off all differences.” Paul: endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

“The body unto which all must turn.” The Qur’án: obey Allah, and obey the messenger and those of you who are in authority; and if ye have a dispute concerning any matter, refer it to Allah and the messenger.
For a thousand years “no individual may presume to breathe a word.” The close of the Bible guards its text in the same way: if any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues.
Moses: ye shall not add unto the word which I command you.
If Bahá’ís contend, “both parties will be in the wrong.” Paul: that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind.
The Qur’án: dispute not one with another lest ye falter and your strength depart from you.

Otherwise each would say “My conscience says it is not good.” Peter to a religious court: we ought to obey God rather than men. When a conscience and an institution collide, what do these readings ask of the believer, and what do they forbid the institution to do to him?

Thoreau would not hand conscience to any assembly: must the citizen ever for a moment resign his conscience to the legislator? We should be men first, and subjects afterward. Is accepting a decision the same as resigning one’s conscience?
“That Body would surely safeguard the Cause of God.” Isaiah: as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest.
Religions divide after their Founders depart. Paul’s farewell: after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
The House of Justice “is under the protection of the Blessed Beauty.” The promise made to the church: the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

“The decision of the majority is the decision of the Blessed Beauty.” Aristotle gave a human reason for trusting a body over its ablest member: the many, when they meet together, may be better than the few good. What do the readings claim beyond that?
“The men of the House of Justice will with great power stop the mouths of the liars.” The Letter to Titus: there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, whose mouths must be stopped.
“Many false traditions and untrue statements will appear.” The Second Letter to Timothy: they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.

Whoever thinks a decision of the House of Justice inapt “has indeed erred.” Mill: all silencing of discussion is an assumption of infallibility. The infallibility here is claimed outright, as a divine gift to a body. What difference does that make to Mill’s objection, and what remains of it?
“The solver of all difficulties.” Solomon’s prayer on taking office: give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people.
Trustees who “have renounced themselves.” Jesus: whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant.

“Ere long will God sail His Ark upon thee,” addressed to Mount Carmel, where the House of Justice now sits. Isaiah: the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains; for out of Zion shall go forth the law.
Its authority, duties and sphere “all derive from the revealed Word.” Isaiah: to the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.
‘Abdu’l-Bahá “conferred the mantle” on Shoghi Effendi. The phrase comes from the parting of Elijah and Elisha: he took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him.

The infallibility of the House of Justice is “conferred,” and a question is asked about decisions made on wrong information. The First Vatican Council also hedged its definition with conditions: when he speaks ex cathedra, defining a doctrine regarding faith or morals. What are the conditions and limits stated in this reading?

Lord Acton, a Catholic, wrote in protest at that council’s work: power tends to corrupt, and absolute power corrupts absolutely. Which features of the House of Justice (election, no individual authority, a written constitution, no power to interpret) bear on his warning?
Members are to see themselves as in the presence of God. Moses to the first judges: ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s.

Subsidiary laws are left to the House of Justice because “the times never remain the same.” Tennyson: the old order changeth, yielding place to new, and God fulfils himself in many ways, lest one good custom should corrupt the world.
Change is “a necessary quality” of this world, so the vessel of law must be renewable. Jesus: neither do men put new wine into old bottles.
The Letter to the Hebrews: that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.
Do not try “to lay down a fixed pattern for future society.” The risen Jesus, asked for the timetable: it is not for you to know the times or the seasons.

The House of Justice may amend or abrogate its own pronouncements. Darius was trapped by the opposite principle: the law of the Medes and Persians is, That no decree nor statute which the king establisheth may be changed. Which parts of Bahá’í law can change and which cannot, and who may change them?
“The last refuge of a tottering civilization.” Yeats in 1919: things fall apart; the centre cannot hold.
Isaiah’s hope for a ruined city: I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness.

The House of Justice holds legislative, executive and judicial functions together. Montesquieu’s maxim, written into most modern constitutions: when the legislative and executive powers are united in the same body of magistrates, there can be no liberty. On what do the readings rely in place of separated powers?
Those who enter the community “have accepted, by their own free will.” Joshua: choose you this day whom ye will serve.

The ineligibility of women for one body “does not constitute” inequality. Paul’s image of a body whose members differ in function and are equal in honour: the body is one, and hath many members. Does a difference of function without a difference of worth persuade you here? What would you need to know?

The wisdom of the exclusion of women from one body “will be fully revealed and appreciated in the future.” Paul on living with what is not yet clear: now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.

numbers-gather-unto-me-seventy-men.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them unto the tabernacle of the congregation, that they may stand there with thee. And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone

deuteronomy-matter-too-hard-for-thee.text: If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, being matters of controversy within thy gates: then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which the Lord thy God shall choose; And thou shalt come unto the priests the Levites, and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and enquire; and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment: And thou shalt do according to the sentence, which they of that place which the Lord shall choose shall shew thee; and thou shalt observe to do according to all that they inform thee: According to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee, and according to the judgment which they shall tell thee, thou shalt do: thou shalt not decline from the sentence which they shall shew thee, to the right hand, nor to the left

chronicles-ye-judge-not-for-man.text: And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city, And said to the judges, Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment. Wherefore now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts

deuteronomy-the-judgment-is-gods.text: And I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God's: and the cause that is too hard for you, bring it unto me, and I will hear it

isaiah-restore-thy-judges-as-at-the-firs.text: And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city. Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness

isaiah-princes-shall-rule-in-judgment.text: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment. And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land

judges-deborah-judged-israel.text: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time. And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment

daniel-law-of-the-medes-and-persians.text: Then these men assembled unto the king, and said unto the king, Know, O king, that the law of the Medes and Persians is, That no decree nor statute which the king establisheth may be changed

corinthians-decently-and-in-order.text: Let all things be done decently and in order

mark-sabbath-was-made-for-man.text: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath

titus-whose-mouths-must-be-stopped.text: For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake

john-my-kingdom-is-not-of-this-world.text: My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence

montesquieu-legislative-and-executive-un.text: When the legislative and executive powers are united in the same person, or in the same body of magistrates, there can be no liberty
montesquieu-legislative-and-executive-un.author: Montesquieu

jefferson-wall-of-separation.text: Believing with you that religion is a matter which lies solely between man and his God, that he owes account to none other for his faith or his worship, that the legislative powers of government reach actions only, and not opinions, I contemplate with sovereign reverence that act of the whole American people which declared that their legislature should "make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof," thus building a wall of separation between
jefferson-wall-of-separation.author: Thomas Jefferson
jefferson-wall-of-separation.work: Letter to the Danbury Baptist Association
